Amy Chen: FYI saw a few blue/green failures where streaming loaders assembled chunks out-of-order but still passed per-chunk checks, later causing subtle kv-cache corruption. digging in.
Anika Rao: can you reproduce reliably? sounds like an assembly/ordering vs checksum gap.
Amy Chen: not 100% reproducible. seems correlated with bundles that have no sidecar manifest and are served gzipped. our range-based reassembly gets non-deterministic latencies and occasionally reorders arrival before final stitch.
Tom Becker: idea: instead of full manifest we can publish a compact 'manifest signature' object alongside the artifact (small JSON + bloom or short xor-sig) that encodes expected chunk ids and order. assembler verifies signature atomically after build. if mismatch -> fail early and fallback.
Jeffrey Lin: i like compactness, but bloom filters have false positives; need to record filter params and a checksum to bound behavior. also think about signed manifest to detect partial uploads (uploads that completed but left older index).
Anika Rao: we can do: stripe_header {stripe_id, chunk_count, byte_windows[], header_hash}. then manifest_sig: {content_hash, header_digest, bloom_hex, version, sig}. assembler validates header_digest first, then uses bloom to quickly check membership before fetching chunk boundaries.
Amy Chen: operationally, what does fallback look like? index-first path still needs to be available as a slower, safer path. runtime should have a quick heuristic: if assembled_order disagrees with header_digest or more than N chunk misses in M seconds -> abort assemble and switch.
Tom Becker: propose parameters: N=3 misses per stripe, M=100ms per-stripe stall, soft-reconcile-window=500ms. If failure within window, start background reconcile agent to pull index-first for missing chunks while allowing existing assembled data to be used for non-missing activations.
Jeffrey Lin: we should also attach a 'reconcile token' to the assembled buffer so cross-node merges can check if buffers are fully reconciled or partial. This prevents kv-cache from accepting partially reconciled buffers as canonical.
Anika Rao: pseudocode:
```
assemble_stripes(stripes):
  header_sig = fetch_manifest_sig(obj)
  if not header_sig: // manifestless
    header_probe = read_first(32KB)
    header_sig = compute_probe_sig(header_probe)
  assembled = stream_assemble(stripes, timeout=soft_quorum)
  if not validate_order(assembled, header_sig):
    log("assembly_mismatch", header_sig)
    background_reconcile(assembled, header_sig)
    fallback_to_index_first(stripes_missing(assembled))
  else:
    mark_buffer(reconcile_token=header_sig)
    publish_ready(assembled)
```
Amy Chen: telemetry to add: manifest_sig_version, header_probe_hash, assembly_mismatch_count, reconcile_invocations, reconcile_duration_ms, fallback_reason. warmup-bot should emit these in the warmup trace.
warmup-bot: warmup: model abc - assembled=86% - mismatch=1 - reconcile_started=true - reconcile_token=sha256:abcd1234
Tom Becker: corner cases: partial uploads where bloom allows but header_digest different; stale caches that serve old header but new chunks; and compressed stripes where byte offsets are meaningless. solution: require header_digest to be authoritative when present; for compressed objects we must store stripe_header_index in object metadata (small) or as a zero-cost sidecar.
Jeffrey Lin: for long-term, Content-Addressed Manifest (CAM) in the registry: store full ordered manifest in registry keyed by contenthash; object stores only a pointer and signature. allows fast verification and atomic rollbacks.
Anika Rao: tests: simulate slow stripe, reorder responses, small header corruption, and bloom false positives. Also unit test reconcile agent to ensure it can safely repair without invalidating buffer usage.
Amy Chen: i'll spin a spike: implement manifest_sig fetch + header_probe + reconcile agent + warmup telemetry. 1-week spike. will post RFC with token format and backend registry changes. cc @Jeffrey for CAM idea.
warmup-bot: job created: manifest-sig-spike (nightly), notify #eng-ml on failures
Jeffrey Lin: also open infra ticket to allow writing stripe_header_index into object metadata for gzip artifacts.
Tom Becker: added note: make assembler idempotent so reconcile is safe to run concurrently. add a short TTL to reconcile tokens to allow GC.
Amy Chen: thanks all. i'll update the docs and link tests once spike lands. closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
